style_when: the story is a product, a device, a price or a market for a thing the reader could buy — an appliance, a panel, a router, a robot arm
prompt: Studio product photograph of a single paper AI usage invoice on a real studio desk surface in a server room, three-quarter angle, the invoice clipped to a matte black clipboard and partly folded to leave the line items unreadable, a softbox key light from upper left raking across the paper with visible falloff, long hard contact shadow to the right, graphite and bone white with a small safety yellow adhesive tab, brushed-steel desk surface, 85mm product lens, shallow depth of field, catalogue clarity, fine film grain, no people, no legible text, no logos.

rationale: The story turns on the invoice itself—the physical artefact where flat spend and falling token price confront a team. A studio product shot treats that invoice as a purchasable object of scrutiny, keeping the frame restrained and focused on the document that carries the cost.
cue: Where the next invoice comes from
subject: a paper AI usage invoice clipped to a black clipboard on a dark desk
core_thesis: AI spending hit a record in October but rose only 1.65% while the price of a million tokens fell 21%, so the flat bill was bought by cutting the size of the work per task, mostly by teams that cannot see token cost as it happens.
core_conflict: Unit price deflation versus unchanged total spend, with use growth hidden by cost-blind teams that shrink work rather than meter it.
composition: extreme asymmetry with the invoice on the right third and long shadow to the left
